_comment: Each entry is one Kalshi 15-minute metals series. Gold and silver are on; copper, platinum, palladium and WTI stay off because their Pyth feeds are not on the trial plan and turning them on gives a 403 and a permanent WAIT. Metals need a working PYTH_API_KEY. The crypto series below use Coinbase and need no key.

engine._shadowSnapshotAtSec: Every window is scored, traded or not: when this many seconds remain the model's fair value and the market's price are recorded, and once the window settles the outcome is written beside them. Two series produce roughly 96 windows a day, which is the only cheap way to find out whether the fair values predict anything.

bot._comment: The bot sends nothing unless you start the server with --live. Sizes are in dollars.
bot._maxEntriesPerWindow: How many times the bot may enter the same 15-minute window. 0 means unlimited, which lets it scalp a moving market repeatedly. Set it to 1 or 2 if fees are outrunning the edge.
bot._strategy: Only enter when fair value on the side being bought is at least minFairToEnter. Take profit once the bid reaches takeProfitCents. Cut the position if the bid falls stopLossCents below the entry. Inside the last holdIfSecondsLeft seconds, stop managing and ride it to settlement, because exiting that late just pays a fee to avoid a coin flip you are already holding.
bot._exitRules: Tiered. A position entered with fair value below takeProfitBelowFair takes profit at takeProfitCents, because a 12c gain is worth a second fee. Above that it rides to settlement, where a 7c gain is not. Either way it is cut if the bid falls stopLossPercent below the entry. holdIfSecondsLeft is 20 rather than 120 so the stop is actually live inside a 5 minute entry window.
bot._maxEntryCents: At 93c you risk 19c to win 7c and need to be right 73% of the time. The fee is small up there but the asymmetry is not, and it is the regime where this model has been most overconfident. Set null to remove the ceiling.
bot._cutting: Exits are immediate-or-cancel limits. Offering at exactly the bid last seen means any tick against you cancels the order, so during a fast move the stop fires, fails, and refires while the position keeps falling. A cut therefore offers cutConcessionCents below the bid, and widens by a cent on each failed attempt up to maxCutConcessionCents. Getting out matters more than the last few cents of the exit price.
bot._maxTotalLoss: A ceiling on cumulative realised losses that does NOT reset at midnight. The daily stop assumes someone is watching; running overnight means a fresh limit becomes available while you sleep. This one halts for good until you raise it deliberately. Set null to disable.
bot._reconstructed: Restored to the settings that were running overnight 17-18 Sep, when the account went from about $41.45 to $49.56. Reconstructed from the trade log rather than a backup, so the values marked uncertain below may be slightly off: entries ranged 73c to 98c (so no entry cap), the lowest predictedFair was about 0.78 (so that was the floor), exits clustered at 90c and above (so a 90c target with no tiering), and stop-outs landed 18-36c below entry, consistent with a 10c trigger plus the widening exit concession.

_cryptoSeries: Kalshi crypto 15-minute windows. 'product' is the Coinbase Exchange product id used as the price source: free, no key, no meaningful rate limit, and no Pyth. These settle on the MEAN of 60 index prices across the final minute rather than a single closing print, which is modelled separately in lib/crypto.js. Coinbase is a proxy for the CF Benchmarks index Kalshi actually settles on, so expect some basis. Use /api/coinbase-check to confirm a product id before enabling it.
